title: Risk Management: The Real Edge
promise: The chapter that separates traders who last from traders who become cautionary tales.
unlock: Work out the gain you need to win back any loss
Use the 1% rule to survive a losing streak
Size any trade from your account, risk and stop
Put the stop where the chart proves you wrong
Pick trades with 2:1 reward-to-risk or better
Check if a strategy pays with expectancy

questions.q: Your account fell from $20,000 to $15,000, a 25% loss. What gain gets you back to $20,000?
questions.why: The gain works on the smaller $15,000. Winning back $5,000 on $15,000 takes about a third, more than the 25% you lost.
questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: Your account is $8,000 and you follow the 1% rule. What’s the most you should lose on one trade?
questions.why: $800 is 10% of the account. A short losing streak at that size would wipe out most of it.
questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: $15,000 account, 1% risk. You buy at $25 with a stop at $22. How many shares should you buy?

chart.label: Price rises to an entry at $25, with a stop at $22

questions.why: Your risk is $150 and each share loses $3 at the stop. 600 shares would put $1,800 at risk: 12% of the account.
questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: You buy at $120 after a pullback. The pullback low was $114. Where does your stop belong?

chart.label: Rally to $125, pullback to a $114 low, then a turn up to $120

questions.why: The idea is proven wrong only if price breaks the pullback low. A stop $1 under the entry sits in the noise; one $30 away makes the size tiny.
questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: Entry $40, stop $38. Which target gives a reward-to-risk of at least 2:1?
questions.why: You risk $2 a share, so 2:1 needs $4 of reward above the $40 entry. The lower targets pay only $1 or $2.
questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

questions.q: You win 30% of trades. Average win $200, average loss $100. Does your strategy pay?
options: Yes: the wins are twice the losses
questions.why: Weight each result by how often it happens. You lose 7 trades in 10, and those losses outweigh the bigger wins.
questions.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: Your account drops from $40,000 to $30,000, a 25% loss. What gain gets you back to $40,000?
retry.why: The gain works on the smaller $30,000. Winning back $10,000 on $30,000 takes about a third.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: Your account is $50,000 and you follow the 1% rule. What’s the most you should lose on one trade?
retry.why: 1% of $50,000. $5,000 would be 10% a trade, and $50 is only 0.1%.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: $30,000 account, 1% risk. You buy at $60 with a stop at $57. How many shares should you buy?
retry.why: Your risk is $300 and each share loses $3 at the stop. 500 shares would put $1,500 at risk: 5% of the account.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: Support runs from $44 to $45. You buy at $47 after a bounce off it. Where does your stop belong?
retry.why: Support fails only if price breaks the bottom of the zone. A stop above the zone gets hit by a normal dip; one far away makes the size tiny.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: Entry $100, stop $96. Which target gives a reward-to-risk of at least 2:1?
retry.why: You risk $4 a share, so 2:1 needs $8 of reward above the $100 entry.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

retry.q: You win 60% of trades. Average win $100, average loss $200. Does your strategy pay?
options: Yes: you win most of your trades
retry.why: A high win rate can hide a losing strategy. Each loss is twice a win, and 4 losses in 10 outweigh 6 wins.
retry.added: New situation written for the Academy

refresher.title: Lesson 1 · The math that ends careers
refresher.text: A loss leaves less money working for you, so the gain back is bigger: −25% needs +33%, −50% needs +100%. Work it out on the smaller account.

refresher.title: Lesson 2 · The 1% rule
refresher.text: Risk at most 1–2% of the account on one trade. On $8,000 that’s $80 to $160, never $800.

refresher.title: Lesson 3 · Position sizing in one formula
Lesson 4 · Where to put the stop
refresher.text: Put the stop where the idea is proven wrong: just below the pullback low or the support zone. Too much risk? Buy fewer shares, don’t tighten the stop.

refresher.title: Lesson 5 · Reward-to-risk
refresher.text: Reward-to-risk = (target − entry) ÷ (entry − stop). Risk $2 a share? A 2:1 target sits $4 above your entry.

refresher.title: Lesson 6 · Expectancy: does your strategy pay?
refresher.text: Weight each result by how often it happens. 0.3 × $200 − 0.7 × $100 = −$10: it loses over time.
